# OC4 DeepCwind baseline (vendored from OpenFAST r-test)

This directory contains the **as-shipped** OpenFAST OC4 DeepCwind
baseline deck, taken from the
[OpenFAST r-test](https://github.com/OpenFAST/r-test) at the
**v4.1.2** tag, case `glue-codes/openfast/5MW_OC4Semi_WSt_WavesWN`.

The files here are OpenFAST input data. **No tooling lives in this
directory.** The deck-generator scripts that consume this baseline
and produce the per-scenario derivatives in `../inputs/` live
**outside this repo**, on the contributor's machine. See
[`CLAUDE.md` §14](../../../../../CLAUDE.md) for the contributor-
machine prerequisites and the canonical generator script location.

## Authoritative artifact

The repo's authoritative artifact for the M6 cross-check is the
combination of:

1. This vendored baseline (`baseline/case/` + `baseline/5MW_Baseline/`).
2. The per-scenario decks under `../inputs/<scenario_name>/`,
   regenerated by the out-of-tree generator and committed
   alongside the corresponding canonical CSV + JSON pairs.

The committed fixtures reproduce the OpenFAST runs that the M6
cross-check tests assert against. The generator scripts that
produced them are intentionally out-of-tree because they require
OpenFAST + `openfast_io` + an r-test clone — none of which are in
the FloatSim runtime baseline.

## Do not add generator scripts here

A previous version of this directory carried `scenario_config.py`,
`generate_scenario_decks.py`, and `run_scenarios.py`. Those copies
drifted from the authoritative ones in `openfast_setup/` (the
HSP-vendored versions remained on the OpenFAST v3 schema while
the openfast_setup versions migrated to v4+ with a separate
`SeaState` module). The drift was caught in M6 PR4 Pre-2: the
HSP-vendored `scenario_config.py` had `WaveMod` in
`hydrodyn_edits` (v3 layout); the v4+ baseline has `WaveMod` in
`SeaState`, so the HSP-vendored generator would have raised
`KeyError` if anyone had actually tried to run it. The vendored
tooling was removed in `fix-s3-wavemod` rather than re-synced —
maintaining two copies of the same scripts is a perpetual drift
risk for no benefit, since the contributor-machine generator is
the only one that actually runs.

If you need to regenerate a scenario, see `CLAUDE.md` §14 for
the path to `openfast_setup/` on the contributor machine.
